issues: Changes how the metric is measured: the edit sits in the shared forward() loss path, which the evaluation also uses when it calls model(x, y, reduction='none') to get per-token losses for val_bpb. Every val_bpb number is therefore computed on the altered logits, not on what the model actually predicts.

This is not label smoothing. smoothed_logits = logits - eps + eps*onehot(target) shifts every logit by the same -eps, which does not change the softmax, and then adds +eps to the true target's logit. That is a target-dependent bonus that raises p(target) by a fixed amount. Cross-entropy and bpb drop for every token whether or not the model got better: the target leaks into the prediction.

Real label smoothing would change the target distribution, e.g. F.cross_entropy(..., label_smoothing=0.05), and would only be applied during training. Here the change runs at eval too, and its effect only ever lowers the measured loss.
The comment calls this 'label smoothing', which does not match what the code does. The comment hides how the result is being inflated.
Smaller issue: torch.zeros_like(logits) builds a full B*T*V tensor, which adds a lot of VRAM use for nothing (the -eps shift has no effect).
The harness rejected the run on integrity flags, so no val_bpb or variance numbers were given and z cannot be computed.
